domain_reasoning: Most time goes into reading the policy wording and loss report and writing up the determination, with the claim system used only to open files and record the result.
length_reasoning: A clear-cut loss under a standard policy takes a few minutes; a loss with exclusions, endorsements or ambiguous facts takes most of an hour.
review_reasoning: The adjuster or supervisor reads the note, checks the cited clause against the policy and the loss facts.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong determination causes a complaint, reopening or a wrongly denied or paid claim; the largest losses can mean financial or regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the insurer's policy forms, claim procedures and authority limits, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Besides talking, the time goes into pulling up the policy and account on screen and entering a note.
length_reasoning: A simple covered/not-covered question takes a few minutes; one with exclusions or a long loss description takes a quarter of an hour.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the recorded call at some speed-up and reads the account note.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong answer on the phone can lead the customer to act on it, causing complaint and rework, and occasionally a dispute over a promised coverage.
context_reasoning: Needs the insurer's policy products and wording conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Checking a program against coding or compliance standards means reading code, configuration and build output and running checks.
length_reasoning: A small build against a short checklist takes under an hour; a large program against a regulatory or detailed standard takes a day.
review_reasoning: A QA lead or developer reads the findings, then opens the code at several flagged places and confirms deviations and suggested fixes.
stakes_reasoning: Missed deviations are usually found later and fixed, but for regulated standards they can create compliance exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's applicable standards and codebase conventions, learned over some weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, time goes into operating the user's software or remote tools and the ticketing system.
length_reasoning: Simple how-to questions take a few minutes; hands-on fixes with remote control take much longer.
review_reasoning: A supervisor listens to or reads the contact and checks the ticket entry.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong fix or instruction costs the user time and is noticed soon; occasionally data is affected.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's standard software, setup and policies, picked up in a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Designing test cases is mostly reading requirements and writing scenarios, steps and expected results as documents.
length_reasoning: A small feature takes an hour or so of case design; a complex feature with many paths takes a full day.
review_reasoning: A test lead reads the cases against the requirements and checks coverage and expected results.
stakes_reasoning: Gaps in cases let defects through to testing or production, usually caught later and fixed.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's features, requirements and test conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Compiling results is reading collected feedback, grouping and writing it up, and logging defects.
length_reasoning: A small round with a handful of testers takes about an hour; a large round with many reports takes half a day.
review_reasoning: The product owner reads the report and spot-checks several findings and the filed defects.
stakes_reasoning: Mis-reported findings cause rework or a wrong release decision, but are reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the product and the test round context, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up account, billing and usage records on screen.
length_reasoning: A simple billing question takes a few minutes; one needing usage history and comparison takes twenty minutes.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the call and checks the account lookup and the note.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong assessment leads to a mishandled complaint or incorrect refund; reversible with rework.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's billing and usage systems and complaint rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Customizing a commercial program means writing or changing macros, templates, configuration or scripts and testing them.
length_reasoning: A small template tweak is quick; a macro or configuration change with testing and release takes hours.
review_reasoning: The IT supervisor reviews the change and tries it in the test setup.
stakes_reasoning: A faulty customization affects users and is caught in testing or by complaints, but one released widely can disrupt business processes.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's applications, processes and customization conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Building a testing tool is writing and testing code.
length_reasoning: A small helper takes a few hours; a framework component through review and merge takes days.
review_reasoning: A code reviewer reads the code, runs it and checks it against the spec.
stakes_reasoning: A flawed tool gives wrong test results, but is found in use and fixed.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's codebase, test infrastructure and conventions, which take months.

domain_reasoning: Investigating involves operating diagnostic tools, system consoles and the ticketing system.
length_reasoning: Many tickets are common problems fixed in minutes; some need long diagnosis and follow-up with the user.
review_reasoning: The help-desk lead reads the ticket notes and checks the fix and closing outcome.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong fix usually recurs and is reopened, but a bad change or lost data can matter.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's systems, setups and standard fixes, learned over weeks.

unit_flag_reason: One test suite for any testing area (regression, negative, usability, database) mixes quite different kinds of work.
domain_reasoning: Writing a suite means authoring test scripts or cases and adding them to the test repository.
length_reasoning: A small focused suite takes a few hours; a regression or database-impact suite takes days.
review_reasoning: The QA lead reads the suite, checks coverage against scope and tries several cases.
stakes_reasoning: Gaps in the suite let defects through, usually found later and fixed.
context_reasoning: Needs the product, its test repository and conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Planning is reading scope and dates and writing the strategy and schedule documents.
length_reasoning: A small release plan takes a couple of hours; a large project strategy takes days.
review_reasoning: The QA manager reads the plan, checks it against scope and dates, and questions assumptions.
stakes_reasoning: A poor plan causes slipped dates or untested areas, which can mean a bad release for big projects.
context_reasoning: Needs the project, team capacity and release history, which take months.

domain_reasoning: Testing a modification means operating the system and test tools and recording results.
length_reasoning: A small change takes an hour; a big change takes a day or more of execution and defect logging.
review_reasoning: The release manager reads the results and defects and checks sign-off against the plan.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong sign-off lets a defect reach production, with outage or data impact.
context_reasoning: Needs the system, test environment and acceptance criteria, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Evaluation is researching tools, reading documentation and writing a recommendation, with trials secondary.
length_reasoning: A quick comparison takes a few hours; a full trial of several tools takes days.
review_reasoning: The QA manager reads the evaluation and checks criteria and conclusions.
stakes_reasoning: A poor tool choice costs money and rework but can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's needs and tool stack, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Preparing a referral is filling in the case details in the ticketing or case system.
length_reasoning: A simple referral takes a few minutes; a complex case with history takes twenty.
review_reasoning: The receiving department or supervisor reads the referral and checks details are complete.
stakes_reasoning: A poor referral delays resolution and is noticed by the receiving department.
context_reasoning: Needs the designated departments and routing rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Reproducing a customer problem involves operating the software, logs and the defect tracker.
length_reasoning: Easy repros take half an hour; hard intermittent problems take a day.
review_reasoning: A developer or support reads the findings and tries the reproduction steps.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong finding sends support or developers the wrong way, but is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's behaviour and history, learned over months.

domain_reasoning: Writing the ticket record is typing notes in the ticketing system.
length_reasoning: A routine problem takes a couple of minutes to record; a long troubleshooting record takes ten.
review_reasoning: A help-desk lead reads the note and checks it covers problem, steps and outcome.
stakes_reasoning: A poor note costs a later colleague some time and is easily fixed.
context_reasoning: A skilled outsider could write the note given what was done; only local ticket conventions are needed.
